general_information.Description: The course is designed as a project-based learning course where students could apply fully-equipped knowledges to design simple real systems based on KITs from manufacturers such as Free Scales, Nouvoton and Phoenix. Students can select one of seven different projects for students to practice in team. Names of projects: 1. Monitoring and controlling room temperature based on ARM Freescale 2. Monitoring and controlling room temperature based on ARM Nuvoton 3.Monitoring and controlling room temperature based on PLC 4. Main Controller for Smarthome based on ARM. 5. Game Controller based on ARM. 6. Traffic light Controller based on PLC. 7. Home weather station based on ARM A programmable logic controller (PLC) is an electronic device used in many industries to monitor and control building systems and production processes. Unlike PCs and smartphones, which are designed to perform any number of roles, a PLC is designed to perform a single set of tasks, except under real-time constraints and with superior reliability and performance. To meet the demands of harsh industrial environments, PLCs are designed to be extremely robust, often capable of withstanding extreme temperatures, humidity, vibration, and electrical noise. Logic controllers are commonly tasked with monitoring and controlling a very large number of sensors and actuators, and are therefore distinct from other computer systems in their extensive input/output (I/O) arrangements. The ARM Cortex-M is a group of 32-bit RISC ARM processor cores licensed by ARM Holdings. The cores are intended for microcontroller use, and consist of the Cortex-M0, M0+, M1, M3, M4, and M7. ARM core processors can support powerful peripherals and connectivity
general_information.StudentTasks: - Students must attend at least 80% of contact sessions in order to be accepted to the final examination. - Student is responsible to do all tasks given by instructor in class or at home and submit on time. - Constantly follow announcements on intranet/CMS at http://cms.fpt.edu.vn for up-to-date course information.

assessments.Grading Guide: Final presentation contains 2 parts: - Slides (team presentations): approx. 20 minutes slides, 20 minutes discussion (5 mins per team member): + Project Objectives + Summarise implementation methods and progress briefly + Design of the product and specification table + Every team member present their own work undertaken - Product Presentation: demonstrate how the design and coding are applied to make the product function properly - Marks will be awarded for the final project based on your team's initiative, the quality of the presentation; the accuracy and correctness of your results; and any suggestions you may make for future work or ways in which you feel you could have developed the experiment further.

assessments.Knowledge and Skill: knowledges and skills in electronics and embedded systems
assessments.Grading Guide: - Assessed by instructor - 04 Progress Reports are required to submit on time + Report 1: at the end of slot 10 + Report 2: at the end of slot 15 + Report 3: at the end of slot 20 + Report 4: at the end of slot 25 - Individual progress reports: defind your own workload, your understandings of project and your progress, approx one-A4 page each report. (Font: Arial, size 10)

assessments.Knowledge and Skill: analysis, implentation process and members' workload
assessments.Grading Guide: - 01 Final Team Report: should describe and assess your team’s efforts: (approx 12-15 pages, Font: Arial, text size 10, including project analysis, implementation process; members' workload and design); and attach source code - Marks will be based on the quality of the report, team work and their own activities
